title: The Forest Dispute
note: Placeholder authored text (owner review pending). A narrative-only quest between people who really work in the settlement: it changes nothing in the simulation. The cast is chosen from existing workers, carriers and soldiers by `cast` (see narrative/quests.py); nobody is created for it.

lines: Share the clearing. Well. I cut the old ones, {planter} marks the young ones with stakes, and neither of us shouts. I can live with that.
You carried it fairly, wizard. I will not forget it.
So the settlement's need counts for something after all. Good. I will still keep clear of the staked ground, I am not a fool, but I will not be shouted at for doing my work.
You backed {planter}. Hm. Then the sawmill goes hungry for a season and I walk further for every log. I hope the saplings are worth it.
You did nothing, then. That is also a choice, wizard. {planter} and I will go on not speaking, and the trees will take care of themselves, one way or another.
That is behind us now, or as far behind as these things go. Thank you for hearing me out.
Back again? Everyone has an opinion on this.
I am cutting what I am meant to cut. The settlement needs timber, and the sawmill and the builders eat it faster than I can carry it.

lines.text: There are {logs} logs in the warehouses and it is never enough.
There is not a single log in the store, and still I am told to wait.

lines: And now {planter} says I am cutting too much. Have you come to tell me how to do my job?

The old trees near my hut were ripe. {planter} has been planting new saplings in the same clearings and says I should leave a stretch alone until they take. I cannot do my work around a field of seedlings.
I may have felled a few young ones in the brush. A pole looks like a tree when you are in a hurry. But the forest is full of trees, and the store is not.

choices.text: What would settle it for you?
lines: A part of the forest I may cut without being shouted at. And a promise that nobody plants on top of my next tree.

choices.text: I will let you get on.
lines: Mind the axe, then.
He agreed to the stakes? Then I will mark the young trees where he can see them, and he will cut the old ones. It is a start. Thank you, wizard.
So timber comes first. I understand it; I plant for the settlement too. I will put the seedlings further from the hut and hope {cutter} leaves them alone.
Thank you. The seedlings thank you too, though they cannot say so. I will keep them staked, and {cutter} will have to cut elsewhere.
You stayed out of it. I hoped for more, but I will not blame you. I will keep planting and {cutter} will keep cutting, and we will see which of us is still here in ten years.
It is settled as far as it will be. Thank you for listening, wizard.
Careful where you step.
Careful. There are seedlings under your boots.
You are the wizard everyone is talking about. If you are here about {cutter}, I will say what I told him: the young trees cannot be cut yet.

lines.text: I plant where the old ones were felled, so the forest comes back. There are {saplings} saplings and poles around me right now, and {cutter} has already chopped some of them.
I plant where the old ones were felled, so the forest comes back. I have hardly anything in the ground yet, and I only asked for a season of leave.

lines: I know he has to cut. I do not know why he must cut *those*.

choices.text: What would settle it for you?
lines: Stakes around the young trees, and a word that he will leave them be. That is all. I do not need him to like me.

choices.text: I will let you get on.
lines: Mind the seedlings.
A shared clearing, stakes and an axe. I never thought I would see those two agree on anything. The lane will talk about it for weeks.
Thank you for listening, wizard.

effects.text: The Forest Dispute: I suggested {cutter} cut only the old trees and {planter} stake the young ones. They agreed to share the clearing.

lines: You backed the axe. The sawmill will be pleased, and {planter} will not, but the store will fill. I suppose that is something.
Thank you for hearing it out, wizard.

effects.text: The Forest Dispute: I backed {cutter}. Timber comes first, and {planter} will plant further away.

lines: You backed the saplings. Then it is a lean season for the sawmill, and {cutter} will not thank you. But the trees will come back, and that is not nothing.
Thank you for hearing it out, wizard.

effects.text: The Forest Dispute: I backed {planter}. The young trees are staked and {cutter} must cut elsewhere.

lines: You stayed out of it. They are still not speaking, and everyone around them has noticed.
I understand why. It was theirs to settle.

effects.text: The Forest Dispute: I left it to {cutter} and {planter}. They are still not speaking.

lines: The forest is as it is. Thank you for your trouble, wizard.
You have heard them both. Well? Everyone wants to know what the wizard thinks.
Have you spoken to them yet? I told them you might.
I was passing the clearing when I saw the two of them, so I know a little. Not much, but a little.

{cutter} with an axe on one shoulder, {planter} with a basket of saplings, and both of them red in the face at the edge of the clearing. I could not tell you who was in the right. I can tell you neither of them was lying.
That {cutter} cuts without looking and {planter} plants without asking. That the sawmill is hungry and the saplings are slow. That somebody ought to say something, and nobody wants to be the one.

choices.text: Suggest they share the clearing: {cutter} cuts the old trees, {planter} stakes the young ones.
lines: I will pass that on. It might work, if neither of them has to lose face.

choices.text: Back {cutter}: the settlement needs timber now.
lines: Timber first. I will say so. {planter} will not like it.

choices.text: Back {planter}: let the young trees grow.
lines: Saplings first. I will say so. {cutter} will not like it.

choices.text: Stay out of it. It is theirs to settle.
lines: As you like. I will not carry anything either.

choices.text: I will let you get on.
lines: Keep your eyes open, wizard.
